title: Solving Hard Problems for Soft Materials with 4D-STEM
content: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is an ideal tool for characterizing materials on the nano- to atomic-scale. The small probe size and multimodal nature of the technique allows this versatile approach to be applied to scientific challenges ranging from biological to physical sciences. STEM can also be performed in-situ to observe how materials change dynamically, including in response to external stimuli, such as straining, heating, and biasing.
